Since his death in 2014, Nash the Slash's career and recordings are being preserved by The Nash the Slash Legacy. His website was relaunched late in 2014, and costumes and instruments were donated to the [National Music Centre](/wiki/National_Music_Centre "National Music Centre") in Calgary. He was declared a Canadian Innovator by NMC and his Vladimir Bosnar custom skull mandolin is on display in the Canadian Music Hall of Fame wing. A distribution deal was signed with Artoffact Records in Toronto in early 2015 to release all six of his albums from the 1980s - *Bedside Companion*, *Dreams and Nightmares*, *Children of the Night*, the rare and previously commercially unreleased live album *Hammersmith Holocaust*, *Decomposing*, as well as *And You Thought You Were Normal*. Artoffact re-released them, plus a download of the "Dead Man's Curve" single, on CD, vinyl and download between 2016-2017. As of 2024, all the physical releases are out of print, but the downloads of all of these titles except *Children* were still available on Bandcamp.

Filming began on a Nash the Slash documentary in early 2017. The film is produced by Side Three Media in collaboration with The Nash the Slash Legacy and is called *Nash the Slash Rises Again!* The film premiered at the 2025 Doc'n Roll Film Festival in the United Kingdom.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

His white tuxedo and top hat will be on display to the public and are being loaned to the [Canadian Museum of History](/wiki/Canadian_Museum_of_History "Canadian Museum of History") in Gatineau, Quebec, for a 2018 exhibit about popular music in Canada from the 1960s to 1980s.

See also: [Cut-throat Records](/wiki/Cut-throat_Records "Cut-throat Records")

The [Staples Center](/wiki/Staples_Center "Staples Center") in [Los Angeles](/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") as used for the 2016 *League of Legends* World Championship final

The various stages of the 2016 Worlds were held throughout the [United States](/wiki/United_States "United States") in [Chicago](/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), [San Francisco](/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), [New York City](/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), and the final in [Los Angeles](/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles").

The groups of teams were decided through a live group draw show on 10 September. The games were played on the 6.18 patch of the game with Yorick disabled, and Aurelion Sol disabled for days 1–3. There were 16 teams and 4 groups that consisted of 4 teams. The group stage was Bo1 and the top two teams from each group would advance to the Knockout Stage. The Knockout Stage was Bo5 and the #1 vs #2 teams from each group would face each other in the bracket. The total prize pool was US$5,070,000 and it was spread among the teams. The first place (SK Telecom T1) took $2,028,000, the second team (Samsung Galaxy) took $760,500, and the third and fourth place (ROX Tigers and H2K) took $380,250 divided among the 2 teams. The rest of the prize pool was distributed among the 5th–16th places.[[37]](#cite_note-s5_results-38)

SKT won 3–2 versus Samsung Galaxy in the 2016 World Championship final, with [Faker](/wiki/Faker_(gamer) "Faker (gamer)") winning the MVP award.[[38]](#cite_note-39) The final was watched by 43 million people, with a peak concurrent viewership of 14.7 million viewers, breaking 2015's final's viewer records.

Reaching Mercury from Earth poses significant technical challenges, because it orbits so much closer to the Sun than Earth. A Mercury-bound spacecraft launched from Earth must travel over 91 million kilometres (57 million miles) into the Sun's gravitational [potential well](/wiki/Potential_well "Potential well"). Mercury has an [orbital speed](/wiki/Orbital_speed "Orbital speed") of 47.4 km/s (29.5 mi/s), whereas Earth's orbital speed is 29.8 km/s (18.5 mi/s).[[112]](#cite_note-Williams2019-112) Therefore, the spacecraft must make a larger change in [velocity](/wiki/Velocity "Velocity") ([delta-v](/wiki/Delta-v "Delta-v")) to get to Mercury and then enter orbit,[[187]](#cite_note-190) as compared to the delta-v required for, say, [Mars planetary missions](/wiki/Exploration_of_Mars "Exploration of Mars").

The [potential energy](/wiki/Potential_energy "Potential energy") liberated by moving down the Sun's potential well becomes [kinetic energy](/wiki/Kinetic_energy "Kinetic energy"), requiring a delta-v change to do anything other than pass by Mercury. Some portion of this [delta-v budget](/wiki/Delta-v_budget "Delta-v budget") can be provided from a [gravity assist](/wiki/Gravity_assist "Gravity assist") during one or more fly-bys of Venus.[[188]](#cite_note-191) To land safely or enter a stable orbit the spacecraft would rely entirely on rocket motors. Aside from the cube, the other four Platonic solids have 4, 8, 12, and 20 faces, allowing for those number ranges to be generated. The only other common non-cubical die is the 10-sided die, a [pentagonal trapezohedron](/wiki/Pentagonal_trapezohedron "Pentagonal trapezohedron") die, whose faces are ten [kites](/wiki/Kite_(geometry) "Kite (geometry)"), each with two different edge lengths, three different angles, and two different kinds of vertices.

Unlike other common dice, a [four-sided (tetrahedral) die](/wiki/Four-sided_die "Four-sided die") does not have a side that faces upward when it is at rest on a surface, so it must be read in a different way. On some four-sided dice, each face features multiple numbers, with the same number printed near each vertex on all sides. In this case, the number around the vertex pointing up is used. Alternatively, the numbers on a tetrahedral die can be placed at the middle of the edges, in which case the numbers around the base are used.

Normally, the faces on a die are placed so that opposite faces add up to one more than the number of faces. (This is not possible with 4-sided dice and dice with an odd number of faces.) Some dice, such as those with 10 sides, are usually numbered sequentially beginning with 0, in which case the opposite faces add to one less than the number of faces.

*One Piece* is the [best-selling manga series](/wiki/List_of_best-selling_manga "List of best-selling manga") in history; in 2012, [Oricon](/wiki/Oricon "Oricon"), a Japanese company that began its own annual manga sales ranking chart in 2008, reported that the series was the first to sell 100 million copies (the company does not report on sales figures before April 2008).[[120]](#cite_note-137) The series had over 300 million copies in circulation by November 2013;[[121]](#cite_note-138) over 440 million copies in circulation worldwide by May 2018;[[122]](#cite_note-139) 460 million copies by December 2019;[[123]](#cite_note-140)[[124]](#cite_note-141) 470 million copies by April 2020;[[125]](#cite_note-142)[[126]](#cite_note-143) and 480 million copies in circulation in forty-three countries worldwide by February 2021.[[127]](#cite_note-144)[[128]](#cite_note-145) It reached 490 million copies in print worldwide by July 2021.[[129]](#cite_note-146)[[130]](#cite_note-147) By August 2022, the manga had reached 516.566 million copies in circulation worldwide.[[131]](#cite_note-148)[[132]](#cite_note-149)[[133]](#cite_note-Guinness-2022-ANN-150) By March 2026, it had over 600 million copies in circulation worldwide.[[29]](#cite_note-ANN-600M-46)[[30]](#cite_note-Natalie-600M-47) By 2004, the brand's merchandise had made more than $1 billion in retail sales in Japan.[[134]](#cite_note-151)[[135]](#cite_note-152)

*One Piece* was the best-selling manga series for eleven consecutive years from 2008 until 2018.[[136]](#cite_note-153) In 2019, the manga did not top the chart for the first time in twelve years, ranking second in the annual manga sales ranking with over 10.1 million copies sold,[[137]](#cite_note-154) although it remained as the best-selling manga by volume in its twelfth consecutive year.[[138]](#cite_note-155) It was the third best-selling manga series in 2020, with over 7.7 million copies sold,[[139]](#cite_note-156) while volumes 95–97 were the 23rd–25th best-selling manga volumes of 2020, behind the first twenty-two volumes of *[Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba](/wiki/Demon_Slayer:_Kimetsu_no_Ya
